label: GO after a rare-rewarded a1 trial (a1->S2 rewarded), agent staying with a1, late in episode
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass), and only when the previous trial was a1 with a rare transition to S2 and was rewarded (prev_reward=1, prev_action=1, prev_common=0 cover ~91% of active steps; the rest are rel -3 GO steps where the previous trial lies outside the window, so they cannot be checked). The agent then picks a1 again (model_act=1 on 99.8% of activations; choice logit moderately positive, 2.8-8.1), i.e. it stays after rare-rewarded, which is the model-free response, not the model-based switch. It never fires at D1/D2, after unrewarded trials, after a2, or after common transitions. Activation also depends strongly on position in the episode: it is silent before about trial 40 and peaks at trials 50-89. That time window is a rough correlate, which is why precision is only ~0.6. Even when every condition holds, many steps stay silent, and I found no observed variable (value, good state) that cleanly separates them. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.20), and I did not find a variable that clearly modulates it. Recorded predicate uses only observed variables plus the current GO choice of the agent.
